title: There is no largest prime
statement: For every natural number n there is a prime p with n < p. Equivalently, there are infinitely many primes.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.exists_prime_gt : ((n : AxNat) -> Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (p : AxNat) => And (AxNat.lt n p) (And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) p) ((d : AxNat) -> ((hd : AxNat.dvd d p) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat d (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat d p))))))

notes: `open` here means NOT ESTABLISHED IN THIS LEDGER; it is not mathematically open, Euclid settled it. It is recorded because it is a live target rather than a curiosity: the prelude already carries `Nat.not_dvd_one_add_mul_of_two_le`, which is exactly the step `no a >= 2 divides 1 + a*t` -- the contradiction at the end of Euclid's argument. 2026-08-17: BOTH missing ingredients have now landed and this fact is one slice from closing. `Nat.factorial` is declared (computation rules definitional, like `Nat.pow`) together with `Nat.dvd_factorial_of_le : (d n : AxNat) -> AxNat.le 1 d -> AxNat.le d n -> AxNat.dvd d (AxNat.factorial n)`, so the number that every positive `d <= n` divides exists in the kernel and `1 + n!` is a witness with no divisor in `[2, n]`. The second ingredient is `F:nat-exists-prime-dvd`: `Nat.exists_prime_dvd : (m : AxNat) -> AxNat.le 2 m -> Exists p, (2 <= p AND forall d, d | p -> d = 1 OR d = p) AND p | m`, admitted axiom-free. Note it did NOT go through `lt_well_founded` as this note previously predicted -- strong induction on `m` would have to DECIDE primality of `m`, a bounded universal quantification whose constructive decision is itself a bounded search, so the search (`Nat.least_divisor_search`) is done directly by ordinary `Nat.rec` on the bound and returns the LEAST divisor >= 2, which is prime for free. WHAT REMAINS is exactly two steps, both small: (1) `1 <= Nat.factorial n` -- factorial is positive, by induction with `one_le_mul` at the successor -- which is what makes `2 <= 1 + n!` and so lets `exists_prime_dvd` be applied to it at all; and (2) the assembly. The assembly: take `p` prime with `p | 1 + n!`; if `p <= n` then `dvd_factorial_of_le` gives `p | n!`, `add_comm` reshapes `1 + n!` to `n! + 1`, `dvd_add_right_cancel_of_pos` yields `p | 1`, and `not_dvd_one_of_two_le` refutes it; so `le_total` leaves `n <= p`, and `lt_or_eq_of_le` turns that into `n < p` once `n = p` is ruled out by the same contradiction. Every lemma named in that paragraph is already admitted axiom-free. formal.statement is written in the SAME core rendering the kernel emits for its own theorems, and uses ONLY symbols `build_nat_prelude` actually declares (checked against the 119-theorem inventory dumped on 2026-08-14), so it can be dispatched without inventing vocabulary. Primality is spelled out inline because the prelude has no `Prime` predicate. Binders carry readable names rather than the kernel's `x0, x1, ...`; that is a pretty-printing difference only, and any admitted proof would render with positional names.
